issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class defines a getter named retrieveQuantity(), but other code (Stock.java and Main.java) expects getQuantity(). This method-name mismatch creates a compilation error and prevents students from using the Stock/StockIngredient API as intended. The problem statement also explicitly asks students to add getters for all private fields, which implies the conventional getQuantity() name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name in StockIngredient consistent with its usages and the problem statement. Replace or add retrieveQuantity() with a standard getQuantity() method (int getQuantity()) that returns the quantity. Alternatively, update callers to use retrieveQuantity(), but the preferred fix is to provide getQuantity() to match conventional getter naming and the solution implementation.

issues.description: The getter for the StockIngredient.quantity field is named retrieveQuantity() in the template but is expected and used as getQuantity() elsewhere (problem instructions request standard getters and other files like Stock.java and Main.java call getQuantity()). The solution uses getQuantity(). This inconsistent identifier naming across artifacts creates a mapping/confusion problem for students (they will see calls to getQuantity() in the template code and problem text but only find retrieveQuantity() in the StockIngredient template).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (and update any references if necessary) so the StockIngredient getter follows the standard 'getX' naming and matches calls in Stock.java, Main.java, and the solution. This aligns the template, problem instructions, and solution naming and avoids compilation/confusion issues.
